## 2. Comprehensive Concept Deep-Dive & Source PYQ Links

### 2.1 Oxidation Number Rules & Redox Titrations (Redox Principles)
- **Exam Weightage**: Tested in **21 PYQs** (Very High Yield)
- **Conceptual Summary**: Rules for oxidation states: Peroxides have $\text{O} = -1$, superoxides $\text{O} = -1/2$, in $\text{OF}_2$ oxygen is $+2$. Disproportionation is a reaction where the same element is simultaneously oxidized and reduced (e.g. $\text{Cl}_2 + \text{NaOH}$). Equivalent weight $= \frac{\text{Molar Mass}}{n\text{-factor}}$. In acidic medium: $\text{KMnO}_4 \to \text{Mn}^{2+}$ ($n=5$); $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7 \to 2\text{Cr}^{3+}$ ($n=6$).

#### Standard Mathematical Formulation
$$
\text{Eq. Wt.} = \frac{M}{n}, \quad n\text{-factor of KMnO}_4: \text{Acidic} = 5, \text{Neutral} = 3, \text{Strongly Basic} = 1
$$

#### Common Traps & KCET Pitfalls
> ⚠️ **Caution Point**: In Caro's acid ($\text{H}_2\text{SO}_5$) and Marshall's acid ($\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_8$), sulphur has an oxidation state of $+6$, NOT $+8$ or $+7$, because of peroxide linkage ($-O-O-$)!

#### Speed Hacks & Problem-Solving Tips
> 💡 **Speed Trick**: Mnemonic for $n$-factors of $\text{KMnO}_4$: 'BAN 153' (Basic: 1, Acidic: 5, Neutral: 3).

#### Linked Representative PYQs:
- **[2026 Shift] Q#1 (MCQ)**: *"$a\text{C}_{2}\text{O}_{4}^{2-}+b\text{MnO}_{4}^{-}+c\text{H}^{+} \rightarrow x\text{Mn}^{2+}+y\text{H}_{2}\text{O}+z\text{CO}_{2}$ $a$ and ..."* — **Correct Answer: A**
- **[2026 Shift] Q#2 (MCQ)**: *"Given below are two statements. Statement-I: In $\text{H}_{2}\text{O}_{2}$ , each oxygen atom is assigned an oxidation number of $-1$ , in $..."* — **Correct Answer: N/A**
- **[2025 Shift] Q#1 (MCQ)**: *"In the titration of potassium permanganate $(KMnO_{4})$ against Ferrous ammonium sulphate $(FAS)$ solution, dilute sulphuric acid but not ni..."* — **Correct Answer: N/A**
- **[2025 Shift] Q#3 (MCQ)**: *"$\text{Match List-I with List-II}$ List-I (Types of redox reactions) List-II (Examples) a. Combination reaction i. $Cl_{2(g)}+2Br_{(aq)}^{-}..."* — **Correct Answer: N/A**

## Critical Exam Traps & Recurring KCET Pitfalls in Redox Reactions

### 1. Speed & 80-Second Constraint Management
KCET demands answering 60 questions in 80 minutes (~1.33 minutes per question). The most lethal trap is spending 3+ minutes on long algebraic derivations. Always check for dimensional consistency or option substitution first.

### 2. NCERT & Karnataka PU Board Direct Lines
Over 45% of KCET theory questions are taken directly from NCERT / Karnataka PU Board textbook summary points, margins, and standard exemplar questions. Pay rigorous attention to exceptions (e.g., electron gain enthalpy of Cl vs F, acidic nature of boric acid, non-polar symmetrical geometries).

### 3. Unit Conversions & Prefix Overlooks
Units of molar conductivity (S cm^2 mol^-1 vs S m^2 mol^-1), micro/nano multipliers (10^-6, 10^-9), and centimeter-to-meter conversions in optics and gravitation account for the highest frequency of careless mark losses in KCET.

### 4. No Negative Marking Advantage
Since KCET has NO negative marking, never leave any question unattempted. When down to two options, use dimensional elimination or parity checks to maximize expected score.
